historical_references.reference: The name Shuqair is derived from the Arabic word 'shuqūr' which means 'thorny'. It is believed that this name was given to a location due to its rocky and rugged terrain. The first historical reference to Shuqair is found in the early Islamic period, during the caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab (634-644 AD) when a battle was fought between the Muslims and the Byzantines near this place.

Another historical reference to Shuqair is found in the 11th century when the Crusaders built a castle here. The castle, known as Chastel Neuf, was one of the strongest fortifications in the Crusader states. It was held by the Hospitallers until 1270 when it was taken by the Mamluks.
